def min_service_cost(parent, weight, time):
    """
    One machine must perform n jobs, numbered 0..n-1, one at a time with no
    idling and no preemption.  Job i takes time[i] seconds.  Some jobs have a
    prerequisite: parent[i] is the index of the single job that must FINISH
    before job i may START, or -1 if job i has no prerequisite.  The parent
    links form a forest (no cycles; parent[i] != i).

    If job i finishes at time C_i (measured from 0, so the first job scheduled
    finishes at time equal to its duration), the total cost of a schedule is

        sum over i of  weight[i] * C_i .

    Return the minimum possible total cost over all orderings of the n jobs
    that respect every prerequisite, as a Python int.  (The minimum value is
    unique, so no tie-breaking is needed.)

    Input domain:
      * 1 <= n <= 200  where n == len(parent) == len(weight) == len(time)
      * parent[i] is -1 or an integer in [0, n) with parent[i] != i, and the
        parent links are acyclic (they form a rooted forest)
      * 0 <= weight[i] <= 10**6   (integers)
      * 1 <= time[i]  <= 10**6    (integers)

    Output: a single non-negative int (exact; fits easily in a Python int).

    Note: greedily scheduling, among currently available jobs, the one with
    the best weight/time ratio is NOT optimal (see the third example, where
    that strategy yields 1332 instead of 1240), and trying all valid orders
    is hopeless for n = 200.

    >>> min_service_cost([-1, -1], [1, 10], [5, 1])
    16
    >>> min_service_cost([-1, 0], [1, 10], [5, 1])
    65
    >>> min_service_cost([-1, 0, -1], [1, 100, 10], [10, 1, 2])
    1240
    """
